timeline.label: Founded in Tokyo to carry small-manufacturer skills to the next owner.
Founder Eiichi Arai (新居英一) held 65.54% of shares outstanding. Free float was 29.06%.
Filed the fiscal 2025 securities report. Policy remains no dividend while the company is still acquiring.
Half-year sales 13,486 million yen and adjusted EBITDA 2,992 million yen. Net debt 5,336 million yen, 1.33 times the 4,000 million yen EBITDA forecast.
Subsidiary agreed to buy Sanko Giken Kogyo. The purchase price is not in the subsequent-event note.
Full-year forecast left unchanged: sales 23,000, adjusted EBITDA 4,000, adjusted profit 2,000, all million yen, and still excluding 2026 acquisitions.
Company said it does not plan to issue shares, pay a dividend, sell subsidiaries, or move to the Prime market.

industry.structure: Japan has a large pool of profitable small manufacturers whose owners are aging. Buyers who will keep the company are scarce relative to private-equity buyers who must sell.
industry.share_shift: The company says inbound opportunities rose after the listing and that it closed three acquisitions in fiscal 2026 through July, including its first carve-out.
industry.trend: The succession shortage is the demand. Financing is still cheap enough that the company funds deals mainly with debt at the subsidiary and keeps consolidated net debt near 1.3 times its EBITDA forecast, below its own 3 to 4 times range.
